caption:
Every quadratic question on the SAT wants one of four things: the zeros, the maximum, the minimum, or where the curve meets a line. Desmos hands you all four if you know where to click.

Save this for test week. Seva's practice tests have the same calculator built in, so you can drill the clicks until they're automatic. Free trial, link in bio.

#SAT #SATprep #SATmath #desmos #augustSAT #digitalSAT #sattips #testprep

slides.title: Type it in standard form, then click the curve
slides.caption: On the test this reads: what are the solutions to $x^2 - 6x + 8 = 0$? Type the equation, click a grey dot, and the label appears. Your answers are $x = 2$ and $x = 4$.

slides.title: The peak is already a point
slides.caption: When a question asks for the maximum value of $y$, click the peak. The label $(2, 11)$ gives you both parts: the maximum value is $11$, and it happens at $x = 2$.

slides.title: The vertex sits halfway between the zeros
slides.caption: In factored form the zeros are $3$ and $-7$, so the vertex sits halfway between them at $x = -2$. Click the low point: the minimum value of the function is $-25$.

slides.title: A quadratic and a line cross twice
slides.caption: A system question shows you both equations and asks for the point $(x, y)$ that satisfies both. Type them in exactly as written. The circled crossings are your solutions: $x = 1, y = 5$ and $x = 4, y = 8$.
